narrative.overview:
Imagine City is a manga zine printed on cool paper. The city behind every screen starts as black-and-white line art: ink strokes, flat white faces, registration crosses scattered across the sky. Each answer paints one building in the chosen major's color and lets more of the hot-pink and mint wash and halftone dots show through, until the reveal screen shows the whole city in color. Interface pieces sit on top of the city like pasted-in zine panels: white boxes with thin ink borders, HUD corner brackets, black hex-ended buttons.

The system is light, loud only where it has earned it, and phone-first. Ink does the structural work: borders, keys, counters, focus rings, selected states. Pink and mint act as paint. They mark the button outline, link underlines, list markers, hover tints and the city wash, and they never carry text. The five major colors are the story's reward and appear only where a major is meant. This world replaces the dark night-city quiz card it grew out of; the dark ground is not coming back.

Motion keeps the "comic panel" feel. Cards rise in and sink out, the picked answer bursts into particles of its major color, a building fills with paint, and cutscene stickers tilt into place. Under reduced motion, all of it becomes short fades, and the color still returns.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground (#f4f2f7) under a code-drawn line-art city that gains color with every answer
Ink borders at 1.5px on white panels, with 3px ink HUD corner brackets at top-left and bottom-right
Black hex-ended buttons outlined in a mint-to-pink gradient
Squared techno display type (Chakra Petch) set italic and heavy for headings; Bai Jamjuree for Thai body copy
Answer rows keyed ก ข ค ง จ in black squares
Ink focus rings on every interactive element
Major colors used only as major signals: meter segments, picked answers, painted buildings, result chips, score bars

rules.name: The Paint Never Talks Rule
rules.body: Pink and mint are paint, not type. They never color text. Pink on paper is only about 2.9:1, so anything that must be read or focused uses ink.

rules.name: The Major Means a Major Rule
rules.body: A major color appears only where that major is meant: an answer that scores it, a building it painted, or a result that names it. Never use it as decoration or as a general accent.

rules.name: The Italic Is for Headings Rule
rules.body: Italic Chakra Petch is reserved for headings (h1, h2, pass sub-head). Labels, buttons and counters stay upright so they read as interface, not story.

rules.name: The Thai Leading Rule
rules.body: Thai stacks vowels and tone marks above and below the line. Keep body text at 1.6 or more (the story pick chip uses 1.75) and never tighten headings below 1.25.

rules.name: The Line Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Cards, buttons, options and inputs carry no shadow. Separate them with a 1.5px ink border, never with a drop shadow, glow or hard offset block.

dos: Do build every new surface on cool paper with white panels at a 1.5px ink border and 6px radius, with HUD brackets on the primary panel.
Do use the black hex button with the mint-to-pink outline for primary actions, and the ink-outlined ghost for secondary ones.
Do use the 3px ink focus ring (`--focus`) on every interactive element, with an offset of 2–4px.
Do confirm selection with more than color: a thicker border, an icon or inverted fill, and `aria-pressed`.
Do draw icons as inline SVG ink strokes at weight 2.4.
Do keep hover effects inside `@media (hover: hover)`, and replace movement with short fades under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do keep major colors tied to their major exactly as defined in `data.js` MAJORS.
Do leave art slots for the team's illustrations and let them collapse cleanly when the file is missing.
donts: Don't set text in pink or mint, and don't use pink for focus rings (about 2.9:1 on paper).
Don't use a major color as decoration or as a general accent.
Don't give cards, buttons or controls drop shadows, glows or hard offset shadows. Only the cutscene sticker lifts.
Don't round buttons into pills. Pills are only for counters and the step indicator.
Don't bring back the dark night-city ground this world replaced.
Don't invent an SDM logo, institutional name or official colors until the real brand assets are supplied.
Don't draw or copy character art in code, and don't write cutscene text that isn't in the brief.
Don't let dev-mode placeholders reach players.
